newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Overbought NYMEX gasoline could tip balance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Overbought NYMEX gasoline could tip balance.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - JULY 29 -------------
* NYMEX gasoline is looking ready for an extended technical correction to lower numbers, RSI's are very overbought.
* Crude has little in the way of technical support and has been helped higher recently by gasoline and therefore remains vulnerable to any weakness that gasoline may bring.

Overbought NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures, the crude and products market's recent leader, could tip them lower on Tuesday with NYMEX crude showing little in the way of strong technical support, analysts said.
Tom James at Credit Lyonais Rouse in Singapore said, "NYMEX gasoline is looking ready for an extended technical correction to lower numbers, the RSI's are very overbought".

He said gasoline had been leading the market, "Over the past 10-days we have seen a 11.12 percent rise in gasoline futures, followed by a 4.78 percent rise in heating oil on NYMEX and coming close third, (NYMEX crude) rising 4.32 percent".
He recommended placing sell-stops below 63.70 cents on the prompt contract and a reduction in overall length.

Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives Limited said in her daily report, "API numbers due later today are suggesting unfriendly gasoline data which may, in the short term put the brakes on technical strength".

GNI Research said in their daily report gasoline's rise through 65 cents on Monday was constructive, but they said the August contract was becoming increasingly vulnerable from a technical perspective and there may be increases in volatility.

Analysts saw gasoline trendline resistance around 65.10 cents with key trendline resistance at 65.92, though an attempt at this may be unlikely today with the 14-day RSI at 72 percent leaving little room for a buying spree.
Support comes in around $64.50, a previous area of congestion with 63.70 providing key trendline support.

They said the upper and lower trend lines on the spot month continuation chart, starting with June 23's low of 54.85 cents and high 56.30 cents and passing through July 10's 57.30 low and July 17's 62.45 high respectively, are still seen capping and underpinning the market.
Yet this expanding wedge pattern is usually read as a bearish signal.
NYMEX crude has little in the way of technical support and has been helped higher by gasoline, and therefore remains vulnerable to any weakness that gasoline may bring.
Analysts said the price action of Brent has seen crude testing, but not breaking a short term down trend line stemming from May 16's $22.40 high over the past three trading days.
However, technicals remain in neutral to positive with trendline resistance coming in around $19.98 and Fibonacci resistance at $20.12.
Initial support is at $19.60 with key trendline support around $19.23.
Heating oil futures were seen holding limited upside potential but Tom James said "The recent uptrend led by gasoline does not look stable".
He recommended reducing long positions and placing sell-stops below 53.80 cents in anticipation of a fall.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
